title: Billing an opioid antagonist dispensed under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19B as a prescription to the purchaser
rule_summary: A pharmacist or designee who dispenses an opioid antagonist pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19B shall, for the purposes of health insurance billing and cost-sharing, treat the transaction as the dispensing of a prescription to the person purchasing the opioid antagonist regardless of the ultimate user of the opioid antagonist. Unless the person purchasing the opioid antagonist requests to pay for the prescription out-of-pocket, the pharmacist or designee shall make a reasonable effort to identify the purchaser's insurance coverage and to submit a claim for the opioid antagonist to the insurance carrier prior to dispensing the opioid antagonist.
exam_relevance: Tests whose coverage is pursued when the purchaser and the ultimate user differ, that the claim effort comes before dispensing, that a purchaser's request to pay out-of-pocket removes the claim effort, and that the subsection speaks of dispensing pursuant to s. 19B.
exceptions: The reasonable effort to identify coverage and submit a claim is not required where the person purchasing the opioid antagonist requests to pay for the prescription out-of-pocket.
common_confusions: Pursuing the ultimate user's coverage instead of the purchaser's.
Submitting the claim after the opioid antagonist has been dispensed.
Assuming that a purchaser buying for someone else must pay out-of-pocket.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19B on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-14.
